purpose: Test whether bounded Graph navigation improves localization as a multi-domain knowledge base grows; this is not an answer-quality claim.

decisionRules.LOCALIZATION_SIGNAL: At S50, R1 has at least one paired required-source recall win, zero paired losses, and does not reduce required-evidence quote recall.
decisionRules.PARETO_SIGNAL: LOCALIZATION_SIGNAL plus average context tokens <= 1.05x R0 and p95 latency <= max(2x R0, R0 + 100ms).
decisionRules.NO_BENEFIT: R1 has no recall win at any tier and no recall loss.
decisionRules.REGRESSION: R1 loses required-source or required-evidence recall on any question.
decisionRules.ENGINEERING_SCALE_BLOCKER: Either arm performs full-corpus scans whose work grows linearly with corpus size; this blocks a production scale claim even if retrieval quality passes.

interpretationLimits: Stage B Gold has already been revealed, so this is a post-hoc mechanism diagnostic, not blind product evidence.
Additional roots are real multi-domain distractors; they do not add new cross-corpus semantic edges.
A localization win authorizes a new indexed local-subgraph design. It does not authorize default Graph content in the answer Prompt.
Synthetic duplication may be used later only for asymptotic engineering tests, never as product-quality evidence.
